name: World history
description: Major events felt across much of the world, not tied to any one town or country — a broad starting point, shown to everyone regardless of where they lived. Check the facts before you rely on them, and add a second group of your own, scoped to your own places, alongside this one.

events.title: French Revolution
events.text: A revolution in France overturns the monarchy and sets off decades of political upheaval and war across Europe.

events.title: Age of mass emigration
events.text: Tens of millions of people leave Europe and Asia for the Americas, Australia and elsewhere, seeking land or work, or escaping famine, poverty or persecution — the reason many family trees cross an ocean somewhere in this period.
events.note: Check: the span, causes and direction of migration differ a great deal by country of origin. Narrow this to your own family's timing if you can, or add a more specific event instead.

events.title: The First World War
events.text: A war across Europe, the Middle East, Africa and the Pacific draws in more than thirty countries and kills an estimated 15 to 20 million people.

events.title: Spanish flu pandemic
events.text: An influenza pandemic spreads worldwide in the final year of the First World War and after, killing more people than the war itself.
events.note: Check: death toll estimates vary widely between sources, from about 20 to 50 million or more.

events.title: Wall Street Crash
events.text: Share prices collapse on the New York Stock Exchange over the course of a week, triggering a decade of economic depression felt across much of the industrialized world.

events.title: The Great Depression
events.text: A prolonged worldwide economic downturn leaves tens of millions unemployed and reshapes government and society in many countries.

events.title: The Second World War
events.text: The deadliest conflict in history involves more than thirty countries and causes an estimated 70 to 85 million deaths, military and civilian.

events.title: United Nations founded
events.text: The United Nations is established after the Second World War, with the stated aim of preventing future wars and encouraging cooperation between countries.

events.title: The Cold War
events.text: A prolonged standoff between the United States and the Soviet Union, and their respective allies, shapes politics, military service and migration in much of the world.
events.note: Check: historians give different start and end dates for this period; 1945 to 1991 is a common and convenient range.

events.title: Sputnik launched
events.text: The Soviet Union launches Sputnik 1, the first artificial satellite, beginning the Space Race between the United States and the Soviet Union.

events.title: First Moon landing
events.text: Apollo 11 astronauts become the first people to walk on the Moon, an event broadcast live and followed by a large share of the world's population.

events.title: COVID-19 pandemic
events.text: A new coronavirus spreads worldwide, leading to lockdowns, border closures and millions of deaths, and disrupting daily life for almost everyone for a time.
events.note: Check: death toll estimates and the exact end of the pandemic differ between sources; treat the end date as approximate.
